newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand sets measures to boost economy.
newsitem.headline: Thailand sets measures to boost economy.

text.p: Thailand approved a series of tough measures aimed at boosting the economy with the goal of obtaining $12-$15 billion in loans from foreign countries and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), finance minister Thanong Bidaya said on Tuesday.

The measures included the suspension of more than half of the country's 91 finance firms. Thailand also set targets of maintaining $25 billion in foreign reserves, cutting the current account deficit, controlling inflation and hiking the value added tax, he said.
Central bank governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi announced suspension of another 42 cash-strapped finance firms on top of 16 companies ordered to stop operations in late June.

Chaiyawat said the 42 newly suspended firms are among those which have borrowed heavily from the central bank this year. He said the suspension will help ease the state burden in helping these firms tackle their severe liquidity problems.

Thanong said the government had set a target of keeping annual inflation at no more than 8.0-9.0 percent, and hoped to keep gross domestic product (GDP) growth around three to four percent per year for the next two years.

In addition the government planned to cut the current account deficit to five percent of GDP this year and three percent next year, compared to eight percent in 1996. The value added tax will be raised to 10 percent from seven percent for the next fiscal year beginning in October.
